query: The Swan {A first-year has wandered into the reeds too close to the swans' nest. The cob is coming out of the water with his wings up, hissing like a kettle.|The swans are nesting again. The cob has grown, or your memory of him has, and there's a first-year in the reeds.|The cob sees you from across the lake and starts hissing in advance.} Step between them {You step between them with your arms out wide and hiss back. The cob considers this, and decides you are the bigger swan. The first-year runs.|You stand your ground, slowly, talking nonsense in a low voice. He lowers his wings an inch, then another, then goes back to the nest.|He knows you by now, and you know him. You both posture, politely, until the first-year is clear.} {He hits you with a wing like a flung door. The first-year gets away; you get a bruise the size of a plate.|You step in and the cob takes it personally. You retreat across the reeds at speed, honked at.|You take one wing and then a bite on the ankle. The first-year helps you limp home, which seems backwards.} Shout for them to run {"Run!" The first-year runs, the cob chases them twenty yards, and everyone ends up in the lake except you.|You shout, they run, the cob gets a mouthful of their scarf. They don't get the scarf back.|You shout from a safe distance. It works, mostly. The first-year limps into the infirmary with a story they'll tell for years.} Put a ward between them {A pale shell springs up between the cob and the first-year. He beats his wings on it twice, offended, then sails back to his nest with enormous dignity.|You ward the first-year and walk them out of the reeds inside it. The cob hisses at the ward all the way, and the ward doesn't mind.|A ward, and a slow walk, and the swans left in peace. The cob watches you go, and you'd swear he nods.}
